solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make fun of one backing detectives (within law)

indicators.note: within says the following pieces sit inside the word for law

parts.note: a rule is a law
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: backing says the detectives' abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a person who supports police detectives while staying inside the law.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, is the usual crossword source for detectives; 'backing' turns it to DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule is a direct verb synonym for mocking someone.

clue.text: Regularly urge stringent limit

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word urge

parts.note: strict is a synonym of stringent

explanation.surface: Someone keeps pressing for a tight cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of urge, R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict is to limit, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Challenged a heartless rule adopted by theologian

indicators.note: adopted by says the pieces are taken inside the theologian's letters

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of the word rule, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A theologian took up a cruel rule and defied others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle UL from rule; DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the stock theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Dared means challenged, as in daring someone to do something.

clue.text: Boo queen's visit?

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
a call is a short visit

explanation.surface: A jeering cry greets the monarch's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is the term for a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a shrill jeer of disapproval, much like a boo.

clue.text: Symbol of good in ladies?

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for good sits inside the word for ladies

parts.note: the ladies is a women's lavatory, a loo

explanation.surface: A mark of approval is displayed in the women's toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' is the British term for a women's public toilet, also called a loo.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is a company's emblem, a graphic symbol.

clue.text: A drug smuggler with time and charm

parts.note: a mule is slang for a person carrying drugs across a border

explanation.surface: A courier caught with drugs also carries a watch and a lucky trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a trinket worn as a charm against evil.

clue.text: Experts in raised shirt seams

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the run of the words shirt seams

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Skilled tailors are judged on their stitched shirt seams.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden step: 'in' signals it. 'raised' in a down clue reads IRTSEAM bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri, plural of maestro, are masters of an art, so experts.

clue.text: 'Amaze' in two words — and one in one's ear

definitions.meaning: split as a maze, a puzzle of winding paths
the inner ear holds a structure of the same name

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Amaze' into A MAZE and you have a synonym; the inner ear's bony canals carry the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is a maze, and also the name for the complex cavity of the inner ear.

clue.text: Part of eastern Europe once providing most of the competition

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word the

parts.note: a race is a competition

explanation.surface: An old region of eastern Europe hosted most of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrace was an ancient region now split between Bulgaria, Greece and Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace is a historical region in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Plan for rejecting large pastry dishes

indicators.note: rejecting says the whole run of pieces is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: mega is slang for very large
tarts are pastry dishes

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to turn down enormous pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' reverses the whole run MEGATARTS, giving the answer letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme, a synonym for a plan.

clue.text: Horses that add up and beat good odds at last

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to sum is to add
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word odds

explanation.surface: Racehorses that add up winnings and finally beat long odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SUM into MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustangs are free-roaming horses of the American West.

clue.text: One glows, seeing the Queen accept one of her own awards

indicators.note: accept says the royal abbreviation takes the award inside it

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour the monarch confers

explanation.surface: A glowing tribute as the Queen herself receives an honour she usually hands out.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour awarded in the monarch's name, so it is fittingly 'her own'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing piece of coal or wood, a thing that glows.

clue.text: Engineers put back — try to call again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: back says the word for put is read in reverse

parts.note: laid is a synonym of put, as in set down

explanation.surface: Engineers replace equipment and then attempt a phone call once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAID into DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To redial is to dial a phone number again, a telephone verb.

clue.text: Mysterious erotic dancing by last couple of ladies

indicators.note: last couple of picks the final two letters of the word ladies
dancing suggests the letters of erotic moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Women watch a strange, sensual dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' makes OTERIC from EROTIC; the definition sits at the front, not the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means obscure, understood by few, close to mysterious.

clue.text: Design it? I once had concealed lighting

indicators.note: had concealed says the letters are held within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to design something they once kept secretly lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignition is the act of lighting or setting something alight.

clue.text: Standard allowance given to prisoner — a result of arson

indicators.note: given to says the standard and allowance are handed over to follow the prisoner

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
a standard is a flag carried as an emblem
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A convict's regular allowance is withheld after he sets fire to things.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflagration is a huge destructive fire, as arson may cause.

clue.text: New editor on holiday drinking rum went to sleep

indicators.note: drinking says the letters take in the word for rum

parts.note: rum is old slang for odd, strange
off means away from work, as on holiday

explanation.surface: A newly appointed editor drinks rum on vacation and dozes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts ODD inside NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is an idiom for falling asleep.

clue.text: Move abroad supported by the French — lovely!

indicators.note: supported by in a down clue puts the French article beneath
move signals the letters of abroad being shifted into a new order

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Emigrating with French help seems a delightful idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' makes ADORAB; in a down clue 'supported by' places the French article underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and charming, close to lovely.

clue.text: Did this genius change, getting recognised?

indicators.note: change tells us these letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a brilliant mind altered course to gain fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished means eminent and honoured, recognised for achievement.

clue.text: Second fiddle — that's a horrible thing!

parts.note: to tinker is to fiddle about

explanation.surface: Playing second fiddle is an unpleasant position.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is slang for something unpleasant or very difficult.

clue.text: India accepted quote was provoking

indicators.note: accepted says India's abbreviation takes in the word for quote

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: India took up a remark that stirred trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: India's abbreviation here is IND rather than the more usual single I; 'accepted' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Incited means stirred up or urged on, which matches the past progressive 'was provoking' as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: The boss's mistake on termination of labour

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the mistake sits above the next piece

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

indicators.note: termination of picks the final letter of the word labour

explanation.surface: The manager blundered over the end of industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is informal British for a boss or works foreman.

clue.text: A salesman returns it whenever getting a drink

indicators.note: returns says the salesman's abbreviation goes backwards

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
if can stand for whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman brings goods back whenever he has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns REP into PER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Twenty runs — one's keeping count

parts.note: a score is twenty
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket statistician tallies twenty runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer is the person who keeps the tally in a game.

clue.text: What might be left in dishing out rice?

definitions.text: What might be left in dishing out rice?

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for left goes inside the rearranged letters
dishing out suggests the letters of rice being scattered into another order

explanation.surface: A cook wonders what remains after serving up the rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishing out' rearranges RICE into REIC, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something left over from the past, a survivor or remnant.

clue.text: Look good surrounded by Spanish cheer

indicators.note: surrounded by says the cheer's letters wrap around the abbreviation for good

parts.note: ole is the Spanish shout of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A handsome bullfighter is watched amid the Spanish crowd's cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone lecherously, a kind of staring.

clue.text: Clerical habit right for student in congregation

indicators.note: right for student means R takes the place of L

parts.note: a flock is a priest's congregation
L is the learner plate letter, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A churchgoing student finds the priest's dress acceptable in church.
explanation.walkthrough: A frock is the long robe worn by monks and clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A frock is a monk's or priest's long habit, the garment of the clergy.

clue.text: The dark wood, for example, from such a venue

parts.note: night is the time of darkness
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A dark forest seems to emerge from a certain kind of place.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, a wood is a kind of club; the definition 'such a venue' points back at the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is an entertainment venue open late, the place the wordplay builds.

clue.text: Go straight for soldiers' prison record

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers
form is British slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: Soldiers with criminal records try to turn honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' in British slang is a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: To go straight is to abandon crime, an idiom for mending one's ways.

clue.text: A revolutionary on principal source of worry

indicators.note: on in a down-style sense: the rebel and A are placed on top of, after, the word for principal

parts.note: a principal is the head of a school
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel sitting on a headteacher's committee causes anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is a nagging problem, a figurative source of worry.
